title: Crossovers
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l1/steps/0/bo: When a **fast** MA (short period) **crosses above** a **slow** MA (long period), it's called a **golden cross**. The classic version is the **SMA 50** crossing above the **SMA 200** on the daily chart.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l1/steps/0/ti: On this lesson's charts, the gold line is the fast MA and the blue line is the slow MA.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l1/steps/1/bo: The flip side: when the fast MA **crosses below** the slow MA, you get a **death cross**. Both are **late**: since they're built from past prices, they usually happen after part of the move is already done.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l1/steps/2/pr: Tap the candle whose close completed the golden cross.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l1/steps/2/ex: Before this candle, the gold (fast) line was below the blue (slow) line. This big bullish candle yanked the fast MA up and took it above the slow MA for the first time.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l1/steps/3/pr: What happened on the right side of the chart?
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l1/steps/3/op: Death cross: fast line dropped below the slow line
Golden cross: fast line rose above the slow line
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l1/steps/3/ex: After the top, the gold (fast) line turned down and crossed the blue (slow) line. That's a death cross, showing short-term momentum has turned bearish.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l1/steps/4/st: A golden cross guarantees that price will go up from here.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l1/steps/4/ex: No signal is guaranteed. A golden cross only says the short-term average has moved above the long-term one. It often turns out to be false, especially in a range.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l1/steps/5/bo: The 50/200 cross on the **daily** is mostly used to read the **long-term trend**, not as an exact entry point. On lower timeframes, crosses become **more frequent and less reliable**.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l1/steps/5/ti: Treat a cross as a clue, not a buy or sell button.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l1/steps/6/se: When the SMA 50 crosses above the 200, it's called a ___, and crossing below is a ___.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l1/steps/6/ex: Crossing up means short-term momentum is now stronger than long-term (golden); crossing down means it's weaker (death).
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l1/steps/7/pr: Why do MA crossovers usually happen after a move has already started?
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l1/steps/7/op: Because moving averages are built from past prices
Because brokers show the signal late
Because they only work on the daily chart
Because trading volume is always low
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l1/steps/7/ex: An MA is the average of past prices, so it always trails price by a few candles, and the cross happens with a delay too.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l1/steps/8/pa: Fast MA moves above the slow one
Fast MA moves below the slow one
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l2/steps/0/bo: In the **two-MA strategy**, you **buy** when the fast MA crosses above the slow one and **exit** (or sell) when it crosses below. Common pairs: **EMA 9 and 21** for short-term and **SMA 20 and 50** for medium-term.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l2/steps/1/bo: When the **gap between the two MAs widens**, the trend is getting stronger. When they **move closer together**, momentum is fading and the next cross may be near.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l2/steps/1/ti: A cross in the same direction as the higher-timeframe trend is usually more reliable.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l2/steps/2/pr: The fast line just crossed above the slow line, and price is above both. What does the two-MA strategy say?
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l2/steps/2/ex: A bullish cross after a low, with price closing above both MAs, means buy by the strategy's rules. Put your stop loss below the last low, since the signal can still fail.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l2/steps/3/pr: The fast line crossed below the slow line, and price is below both. What does the same strategy say?
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l2/steps/3/ex: A bearish cross after a high, with a close below both MAs, means momentum has turned down. By the rules, you close your long or go short. Stop loss above the last high.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l2/steps/4/pr: You bought on a golden cross and put your stop loss below the last low. What's the risk-to-reward ratio?
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l2/steps/5/st: When the gap between two MAs keeps widening, it usually means the trend is getting stronger.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l2/steps/5/ex: The fast MA pulls away from the slow one when recent prices are quickly moving away from the long-term average, meaning momentum is building.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l2/steps/6/bo: Don't trade crosses blindly. A simple filter: only take crosses that **agree with the long-term MA** (say, the 200). Above the 200, take only bullish crosses; below it, only bearish ones.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l2/steps/7/pr: Price is below the 200-day MA, and on the 4-hour chart the EMA 9 just crossed above the EMA 21. With the trend filter, what do you do?
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l2/steps/7/op: Skip this buy and wait for a bearish cross
Buy, but with no stop loss
Ignore the filter just this once
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l2/steps/7/ex: Below the 200-day, the long-term trend is down, and the filter says take only sell signals. A bullish cross here goes against the bigger trend and is more likely to fail.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l2/steps/8/pr: Put the steps of a two-MA strategy trade in order.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l2/steps/8/it: Check the long-term trend (above or below 200)
Wait for a cross in the trend's direction
Stop loss beyond the last low or high
Exit on an opposite cross or take profit
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l2/steps/8/ex: First the big-picture direction, then the signal, then an entry with defined risk, and finally an exit rule. Entering before the candle closes can fool you with a half-formed cross.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l3/steps/0/bo: In a **ranging market**, the MAs flatten out and **tangle together**. The result is cross after cross, each one quickly reversing. This is called a **whipsaw**, and a crossover strategy racks up loss after loss here.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l3/steps/1/ti: How do you spot a range?
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l3/steps/1/bo: The signs: the **MAs are nearly flat**, price keeps flipping from one side of the line to the other, and highs and lows are **at the same level**. Here, the **edges of the range** matter more than crosses.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l3/steps/1/ti: If two flat MAs are lying on top of each other, set the crossover strategy aside.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l3/steps/2/pr: What's the market doing, and how reliable are the cross signals here?
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l3/steps/2/ex: Price bounces between a fixed high and low, and the two MAs are flat and tangled. Every cross here got cancelled out very quickly.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l3/steps/3/pr: In a month-long range, you took 6 cross signals, and each lost 15 pips on average. What's the total loss in pips?
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l3/steps/3/ex: 6 × 15 = 90 pips. Small back-to-back losses in a range can wipe out the profit from a good trend.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l3/steps/4/st: When both MAs are flat and tangled, cross signals are more reliable than ever.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l3/steps/4/ex: The opposite. Flat MAs mean there's no trend, and the crosses are more noise than signal.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l3/steps/5/bo: A few common filters: the slow MA's **slope** should be clear, price should show **trend structure** (higher or lower highs and lows), and the cross shouldn't be **near the edge of a range**. Many traders also wait for a **close outside the range**.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l3/steps/6/pr: The market is ranging and the fast line just crossed above the slow line, but price has reached the top of the range and left an upper wick. What's more likely?
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l3/steps/6/ex: In a range, the cross usually happens once price has already reached an edge, which is late. Resistance at 1.2750 has turned price back twice, and the upper wick shows selling pressure. A drop back to the middle of the range is more likely.
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l3/steps/7/pa: Direction and strength of the MA
Top or bottom of a sideways market
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l3/steps/8/pr: You spot a golden cross on the 1-hour EUR/USD chart, but both MAs are flat, price is in the middle of the 1.0800 to 1.0850 range, and there have been 4 other crosses this week. What's the best call?
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l3/steps/8/op: Wait until the range breaks or price hits an edge
Buy bigger because it's a golden cross
Sell because the last crosses lost money
Buy and remove the stop loss
lessons/moving-averages-u2-l3/steps/8/ex: Every sign of a range is here: flat MAs, lots of crosses and price in the middle. Waiting is best: either a real breakout from the range, or trading from the edges with a stop loss.
